script.text: Most advanced AI chips are finished in Taiwan. Could a New York factory share that job?

On October eighth, GlobalFoundries announced a five-year deal worth about two billion dollars. At its plant in Malta, New York, it will make silicon interposers for TSMC. An interposer is a thin silicon layer that wires processor and memory chips together.

The packaging method is TSMC's CoWoS, used for AI chips. GlobalFoundries calls Malta the first U.S.-based source of these interposers. Volume production is planned for the first half of 2028. The companies have not disclosed volumes or customers.

Why it matters: industry analysts say packaging, not chipmaking, limits AI chip supply, and one analysis says TSMC holds over ninety percent of this market. This deal covers one part of the process, and 2028 is still years away.
Will U.S. chip packaging catch up with Taiwan? Yes or no?
